target_customer: Startups and growing companies that need to hire without a recruiting team
problem: Founders struggle to recruit while building the rest of the business. Dover first automated candidate sourcing and outreach and now offers a free ATS plus a marketplace of fractional recruiters.
business_model: Free ATS as lead generation, plus marketplace take rate on fractional recruiters (hourly, retainer or pay per hire)

founders.name: Max Kolysh
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2021 says all three founders worked at earlier startups and struggled to recruit. No employers or schools stated.

founders.name: Anvisha Pai
founders.background_notes: Named CTO and co-founder by TechCrunch 2021. Not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: George Carollo
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder at Dover (S19) on the YC page and as COO and co-founder by TechCrunch 2021.

competitors.name: Beamery
competitors.what: Talent CRM and candidate sourcing tool for recruiters, which proactively finds and engages candidates
competitors.funding_then: $2M raised as of June 2016, source predates the batch

technical_complexity.rationale: Candidate sourcing and email outreach automation and later an ATS are standard web software, with the main difficulty being data access to LinkedIn style sources.

defensibility.rationale: Sourcing automation was copyable and dependent on third party candidate sources such as LinkedIn and Indeed. A free ATS creates mild lock in and the recruiter marketplace some supply side lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The ATS and sourcing space stayed crowded, Dover's own site now names Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and Paraform as rivals. No incumbent acquired Dover.

market_need_then: Founders at early stage companies reported hard hiring while building the product, per TechCrunch 2021. Recruiting spend and agency fees are large, making cheap automation attractive.

branding.domain_note: Uses dover.com, which the company owns now. Acquisition history not found.
branding.community_and_virality: Launched a free ATS on Product Hunt, no evidence of wider brand buzz found.

brand_strength.rationale: A recognizable one word name and a free tool brought some inbound, but search results are crowded with unrelated companies called Dover and no press about the brand itself was found.

pivots.from: Recruiting automation for sourcing and outreach
pivots.to: Free ATS plus marketplace of fractional recruiters (Recruiting Partners)
pivots.why: Not stated by a source. A job posting seen in search says the marketplace launched in mid-2024.

outcome_analysis: Dover raised a seed round led by Founders Fund and a $20M Series A in July 2021 led by Tiger Global, then repositioned from sourcing automation toward a free ATS and a fractional recruiter marketplace, claiming 500 plus customers. It remains active with a small team. A possible layoff of about 30 percent of staff appears in one aggregator and is unverified, so the story is a company that adapted after the 2021 hiring boom.
notes: YC page says $23M raised, TechCrunch and Dover blog say $20M Series A, so roughly $3M may be earlier or later capital not identified. Dealroom reportedly lists $125K from YC in 2019-09, one aggregator, unverified. Layoff claim of 23 roles seen only on Scoutify citing layoffs.fyi, unverified. Competitor list is thin because no 2019 dated coverage of rivals for startups was found; only Beamery has a pre batch dated source. Seed amount not stated.
